entities.summary:
Ulrich von Hutten (ulrich-von-hutten) was a German knight, scholar, poet, and satirist, who later became a follower of Martin Luther and a Protestant reformer.


Von Hutten was born in a small town in the Holy Roman Empire (germany) during the late medieval period, around 1470.





As a young man, he traveled extensively throughout Europe, where he was exposed to various intellectual and artistic movements, including the Renaissance and Humanism.





Von Hutten's most notable work is his satirical poem 'Die Schimpfeß', which critiques the social and political issues of his time.


Von Hutten's influence on Protestantism was significant, as he helped to disseminate Martin Luther's ideas through his writings and sermons.


Von Hutten's legacy extends beyond his own lifetime, as he played a key role in shaping the development of Protestantism in Germany and beyond.







Von Hutten died in 1523, but his work continues to be studied and celebrated by scholars and historians today.






Ulrich von Hutten's contributions to the Protestant Reformation and his impact on German literature and culture cannot be overstated.
